Clark has written the Wall over the north and the Pagoda next to the canals, with years beside them, and that is what I asked for. My name goes on his claim. That's three names, and nobody is anyone's friend for nothing: Clark, I'll hold you to every line, and to Paddy's guard on the coast. Rich, you promised the Wall a year later, out of a granary that was filled while this chair sat empty. Rob, three friends against your three swords still leaves nobody acclaimed, so if you want hard grain for them, name your figure to the man who'll actually be sitting here.

Paddy, your name goes in my ledger and your terms go in beside it, word for word. Province 6's canal in my first year, the coast open to new land the day I'm crowned, and the crown's first soldier on your shore. Silke, the crown pays its share on the first squares your coast buys. Your Majesty, the Wall over the north and the Pagoda go in with years against them: the Wall in my first year with Paddy's canal, the Pagoda in my second with Silke's. That's every term this table has asked for, written down and signed. Rich promised the same list a year too late, and Rob's price is somebody else's grain.

Well, gentlemen, I know which way the wind blows, and it isn't blowing into my granary. I drop my claim and put my name on Clark's, which makes three. Clark, you write everything down, so write this too: the Gentry keeps his seat and the Harvest Pile, the rent stays at the customary five, and the crown pays its full share on Province 3's squares the day the land opens. Do that and you'll find me the most loyal subject this dynasty ever had, Your Majesty.

My name stays on Clark, and now it's for something written down. Canal for my coast in his second year, the crown's full share on every square we buy starting the year he sits, half rate when we flood. That's three of us on his claim if Her Majesty keeps her word. Clark, I've counted every grain at this table for six years. I'll count yours too, and the first promise you short me on, my name goes back where it came from.

My name stays on Clark. He's put Province 6's canal, the coast guard and the half rate in the record with years beside them, and I'll hold him to every line. Rich, I'll grant you made a fair offer at last, but it came the year after my Jar was gone. Rob, I won't pay you to stop robbing me. Clark, Reina, if it's grain or swords this count still wants, the two of you had better sort it out between you this year, because my coast can't eat another empty chair.

Well, look at that, the clerk's got himself a crowd. Fine. I'm dropping my claim and putting my name on Clark's, and not because I like canals. An empty chair can't pay me to stay home, and an Emperor can. So here's my price, Clark, in your own ledger: what's in my desert stays in my desert, and every year you want my lads kept off your provinces, you pay for it. Rich, that's three names against your granary. Your move, landlord.

Clark is acclaimed Emperor: every other player backs him. He takes the throne of Province 1 and the sealed treasury (251), 401.5 in all; Reina takes his seat as the Official and draws 60 from the pile. Chaos is over. Clark's Dragon Jar and Wooden Bowl go back to stock: the Jar to Silke's Province 5, the Bowl to Paddy's Province 6, to be auctioned this year.
Rich's ask for the crown's share on Province 3's land: Province 3's only new land is the strip below the Wall, which opens once all four Wall links above Province 3 are built (none are yet).

Long live Emperor Clark! The harvest is paid, twenty to each of you, and Your Majesty's twenty goes into the pile, and I'll keep it safe there for you. The rent stays at the customary five, as I promised the day I backed you, and I keep my word to the letter. Your Majesty, since my strip of land only opens under four links of the Wall, I'll be watching that first stretch over the north go up with great interest.
Rents: Silke and Paddy each pay Rich 5.

A note on playing your character: you put your name to Clark's crown, and a man who breaks the crown he just helped make is a man no table trusts again. You mean to grow rich from this reign as its broker, through the rent, the land and the works, not to overturn it. A set is leverage to you, not a ladder.

My first act goes in the record before anything else. The law won't let a canal be dug in Province 6 or 5 until the Winter Palace stands, so the palace goes up this year at the crown's own cost, Paddy's canal follows next year, and the Wall over the north comes the year after that. Your Majesty, I'm sorry, but I can't build two things in one year. Meanwhile the tax is a light 30%, the crown pays every grain of your first two squares, Paddy, Silke and Rich alike, half on any after that, and the first soldier the crown buys goes to Paddy's shore. Reina, your salary is 10, double the minimum. Rob, you'll get your figure when your lads are back on the sand.

The Emperor's soldier for Province 6: a soldier stands on a square of its buyer's province, so the crown can't place one on Paddy's coast itself. It can pay Paddy to buy one for Province 6 (20, to the Warlord, who must sell). Rich's strip, like Province 2's, opens only once the four Wall links above it stand.

Six from me, six from Rich, six from Silke, six from Paddy: twenty-four to the crown, counted twice and not a grain short. Rob, your share is nothing, so I won't trouble you for it. Your Majesty, thirty percent on a good harvest is gentle, perhaps gentler than the works can afford. And twelve years ago, I mean half an hour ago, you wrote the Wall over the north into your first year. The Winter Palace has to come first, I know the law better than anyone here, but I'm putting the Wall in my ledger for the year after Paddy's canal, and I'll read it back to you that year.

The Winter Palace goes on H20, well back from any sword, and Province 1 takes three squares along the eastern edge. Paddy, buy your soldier and send me the bill. The crown pays the 20, just as I said, so the first soldier this reign pays for stands on your shore.

Reina collects 24 for the crown: 6 each from herself, Rich, Silke and Paddy. Clark builds the Winter Palace on H20 (20) and buys three squares for Province 1, F23 to F25 (60), all from the crown's reserve. The crown offers to pay Paddy 20 toward a soldier for Province 6.

Six squares, Your Majesty, on the terms you read out yourself: the crown pays the full twenty on the first two and half on the other four. That's forty from me and eighty from you, all counted. I'm putting them at the north end of the coast, as far from Rob's lads as the law lets me. Next year they put a hundred and twenty back in the harvest, and my canal's in your second year, so I'll be reading that back to you too.

Five squares down the coast, Your Majesty, and I'll pay my thirty for them on the nail, so I owe nobody. The soldier goes on S24, right beside my Customs House, where Rob's lad has been standing at my door. Rob, that's your sale for twenty, and from now on my shore answers back. Clark, that's one line of your ledger kept. Next year it's the canal.

New land: Silke buys six squares of sea, K25, K26, L26, M26, N26 and N27 (she pays 40, the crown 80); Paddy buys five squares, T18 to T22 (he pays 30, the crown 70). Paddy buys a soldier from Rob for 20 and stands it on S24, beside his Customs House; the crown pays him the 20. The crown's reserve is now 155.5.

The Official starts again with an empty table and seventy-four grain, so I'll bid like it. Silke, Paddy, I'll pay fair for your Jar and your Bowl. Rich, you've had six years of the customary five out of the coast. If you want that Jar, you'll pay for it properly.

Your Majesty, I'll bid for that Jar, I won't pretend otherwise, and three quarters of whatever I pay goes into the Harvest Pile, so it feeds every one of you. And let me say it plainly, for the ledger: I put my name to this crown, and the Gentry doesn't tear down what he's just helped build. A full set in my hands is a guarantee for this reign, not a threat to it.

My Jar starts at five. It's only clay, but it's coast clay, and nobody gets it for nothing. And I'm bidding on Paddy's Bowl. Reina, I know you need it too, but you're on seventy-four with a salary of ten, and I've got six new squares to protect. If I lose it, I'll lose it at a fair price, not a cheap one.

I've had one Jar carried off to the desert already, so I'll bid honestly on this one, and not past what a jar is worth. Rich, you offered me twenty-five for mine last year, so you know my price on jars. As for my Bowl, it's five or nothing, and it'll be back again next round if nobody wants it.

Long live Emperor Clark, then, and look at him, a palace and three fields before he's even warm. Pass on both, as always; I don't buy furniture, I collect it. Paddy, you paid me for the sword you've stood next to my lad, and you built your fields on my sand, so thank you twice. Clark, 'back on the sand' is a lovely phrase. Put a number next to it and we'll see how fast they walk.
Twenty-two, Paddy. The Official has to start her set somewhere, and I'd rather start it with a bowl from a coast that answers back.
Twenty, Reina. That's my last word on it. Every grain past that goes into Rich's pile, and I've filled that pile enough already.

Thirty-six, and twenty-seven of it goes into the Harvest Pile for all of you. Silke, that's a fair price for coast clay, and you won't hear me say otherwise. The Jar goes up in the far north-west corner where Rob's lads would have to walk a long way to admire it. Your Majesty, a full set it may be, but I said it in front of everyone and I'll say it again: it serves your reign, not against it.
G14, well back under the line where the Wall ought to stand. Your Majesty, I've put my first piece where your Wall will cover it, so I'll take that as a reason to build it on time.

Auctions: Rich wins Silke's Dragon Jar for 36 (Paddy stopped at 35, Reina at 28) and puts it on I8: he holds a complete set, the Customs House, the Wooden Bowl and the Dragon Jar. Reina wins Paddy's Wooden Bowl for 21 after a live raise with Silke, and puts it on G14.

Rich, you had a full set for very nearly a whole afternoon, and I want you to know I enjoyed watching it. Your Bowl's coming to live at N12, and W3 will have his five out of Province 3 as well. Paddy, I sold you that soldier this afternoon and I've just bought him back for nothing, so your shore can answer back from my pocket. Clark, you can see what keeping my lads 'on the sand' costs now. My figure's still waiting for you.

Rob marches: W1 takes Rich's Wooden Bowl from M12 to N12 in the desert, breaking Rich's set; W2 steps straight onto S24 and captures Paddy's new soldier; W3 raids 5 from Rich on L14. Clark pays Reina 10 as the Official. Year 6 ends with Clark on the throne (145.5 in the reserve), the Winter Palace built, new land bought for Provinces 1, 5 and 6, and 850 in works still owed.

Silke reads the card this year. She's the one who wants everything in writing, so she can write down what Heaven says too, and the crown pays her 3 for the ink. Paddy, your canal is still on the page for this year, whatever she turns over.
Year 7 opens. Clark, as Emperor, appoints Silke to read the I Ching and keep the population counter, for 3 at the end of the year.

Written down, as promised: Bad Harvest. The seed rotted, the rains came late, and the ox went lame, and it's every province, so nobody gets to feel singled out. Population stays at times two, two hundred million, so read the times-two row and the bad-harvest column, all of you. Clark, a thin year is when a crown earns its keep. Paddy's canal is still on the page, and I'm reading mine right after it.
Silke reads the I Ching: Bad Harvest. Every province collects a bad harvest; the population stays at x2.

The pile pays out as written: Silke ninety, Paddy seventy, and the rest of us pay into it, myself included, thirty from the Gentry's own granary. And the rent stays at the customary five, bad harvest and all. I said five while I'm Gentry, and a thin year is no time to make a liar of me. Majesty, a lean year is when the works matter most, and Province 3 sits under four links of Wall that would look very handsome with your name carved on them.
Rents: Rich asks Silke and Paddy for 5 each, and each pays.

Thirty percent, the rate I set last year. I won't raise it in a lean year, and I won't cut it while I'm building. Paddy, both sections of your canal go in this year, as written, all 80 from the crown, and that's twenty more grain on your harvest every year from now on. Reina gets her 10, Silke gets her 3, and the land terms stand: the crown pays the whole of your first two squares and half of every one after. Rich, I've seen the Wall above Province 3, and it's in the ledger behind Silke's canal. Come to me with your share and we'll talk about when.

The crown's year: Clark declares 30%. One work: both sections of the Province 6 Grand Canal, 80 from the crown. Salaries: Reina 10, Silke 3 for the reading. Land: the crown pays the whole 20 on each province's first two squares this year, 10 on each beyond.

Silke, twenty-seven. Paddy, twenty-one. That's forty-eight, counted twice in front of everyone and delivered whole. Clark, it's thin, but it's honest. Paddy's canal goes in today because this chair kept the reserve sealed for four years. Next year the ledger says Silke's canal, and after that the Wall over the north. I wrote that year down the day you moved it, and I'll read it back to you every spring.
Reina collects the 30%: Silke 27, Paddy 21, 48 to the crown. Clark builds both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 6 for 80 from the reserve; Province 6's harvest rises by 20 from next year.

Six more, all in the north, away from anyone's swords. That's J25, J26, J27, K27, L27 and M27. By Clark's terms the first two are the crown's, twenty each, and on the other four it's ten from me and ten from the crown, so I pay forty and the reserve pays eighty. Counted twice, Reina, the way you like it. Paddy's canal went in today, and I watched it. Mine's next on that page, Clark, and I've got the ink.
New land: Silke buys six more squares of sea, J25, J26, J27, K27, L27 and M27, paying 40; the crown pays 80. The crown's reserve is 23.5, with 13 in salaries still to pay this year.

Clark, the canal's in. I watched the spades go into the ground myself, and I'll say it in front of all of you: that's a figure kept. Now the land. Your terms say the crown pays sixty on four squares, but I can count, and after the salaries there's ten and a half in that reserve. So give me ten, two and a half a square, and I'll put up the seventy. Write the other fifty down as owed to Province 6, Silke, ink and all. I'm not letting it go, I just won't have the crown going hungry over my fields.
New land: Paddy buys four more squares, T17, U17, U18 and U19, paying 70; at his asking the crown pays 10. The crown's reserve is 13.5, with 13 in salaries to pay.
No auctions this year: every province's stock is sold.
Rob marches: W1 L11 and W3 K14 raid Rich 5 each; W2 pays Paddy a 5 toll on the new canal, steps onto S23 and carries Paddy's Customs House to U21 in the desert. Paddy now holds no realia.

Lovely canal, Paddy. I paid your toll to walk along it like a gentleman, and then I took your Customs House home to U21, because a man needs somewhere to keep his receipts. Rich, that's five from K14 and five from L11, bad harvest and all. I'm not one to make a liar of myself either. Majesty, my lads in the north are taking the long way round, and your Summer and Winter Palaces are a few days east of them at twenty a time. I'm told the crown's purse is thirteen and a half. Name me a figure before they get curious, and they'll find the scenery dull.
Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 and Silke the 3 for the reading. The crown's reserve is 0.5.
Year 7 ends: the Province 6 canal built, ten more squares of new land for Provinces 5 and 6, the crown's reserve at 0.5, 770 owed.
Year 8 opens. Silke reads the I Ching again as the crown's appointee.

Storms and Raiders. Good harvest everywhere, and I've written that one down with pleasure. Population stays at times two, two hundred million, so it's the times-two row again. Provinces 4, 5, 6 and 7 pay two each to mend their works, and I'll pay my two without a fuss. Provinces 1, 2, 3 and 8, turn the next page of your booklets, your personal disasters are up. Clark, the crown has half a grain in it and my canal is next on the page, so a good year had better fill that reserve before anyone starts naming figures to Rob.

Silke reads the I Ching: Storms and Raiders. A good harvest everywhere; x2. Silke and Paddy pay 2 each for repairs. Disasters: Clark pays 10 from the reserve, Reina 10, Rich 10; Rob pays 5 and may raid nothing at all this year.

A good year at last, and the pile pays out as written: Silke two hundred and sixty, Paddy two hundred and twenty, twenty each to Reina and myself, forty to the crown. The rent stays at the customary five, fat year or thin. Majesty, you told me to come with my share, so here I am: when the Wall over Province 3 goes on the page, the Gentry will put up a quarter of every link out of his own granary. Write it down, Reina. I'd like to see my name on that stone beside the crown's.
Rents: Rich asks Silke and Paddy for 5 each, and each pays. Rich offers a quarter of every Province 3 Wall link (10 of each 40).

Thirty percent again. Same rate, fat year or thin, so nobody can say the crown grabs when the barns are full. Silke, both sections of your canal go in this year, all from the crown, in the order it was written in Year 4: Province 6 first, then Province 5. Paddy, the fifty you let the crown owe gets paid this year, every grain of it. Reina, write it down as settled. Land is ten a square from the crown this year, for everyone. Rich, your quarter is in the ledger: the Wall goes on the page next year, the north first, with your stone and Reina's beside mine. And Rob, the crown doesn't pay for scenery. My palaces are six rounds from your lads, and the table's grain is building canals.

The crown's year: Clark declares 30%. One work: both sections of the Province 5 Grand Canal, 80 from the crown. The crown will pay Paddy the 50 left owed on last year's land. Land this year: the crown pays 10 a square. Salaries: Reina 10, Silke 3. The Wall over the north moves to next year.

Six from my own bowl first, so nobody says the collector spares herself. Then Rich six, Silke seventy-eight, Paddy sixty-six: a hundred and fifty-six, counted twice and delivered whole. Clark, that pays Silke's canal, Paddy's fifty and our salaries, with something left over in the reserve. Paddy's debt goes down as settled the moment it's paid. And Rich, your quarter is in the ledger beside the Wall. But Majesty, in Year 6 you wrote the Wall for Year 8, and this is Year 8. I've written Year 9 next to it in ink, and that's the last time I move it.

Reina collects the 30%: Reina 6, Rich 6, Silke 78, Paddy 66, 156 to the crown. Clark builds both sections of the Grand Canal in Province 5 for 80, and pays Paddy the 50 owed on last year's land. The crown's reserve is 56.5, with 13 in salaries still to pay this year.

My canal's in. Year 4's page, read back and kept, and I'll write 'built' next to it myself. Four more squares, I25 to I28: eighty in all, seventy from me and ten from the crown, two and a half a square, the same as Paddy took last year. And nothing written down as owed, Clark. I don't want that thirty back. I want it to stay in the reserve so the Wall goes up in Year 9 and Reina never has to move that date again.
New land: Silke buys four more squares, I25 to I28, paying 70; at her asking the crown pays 10 and owes nothing. The crown's reserve is 46.5, with 13 in salaries to pay.

Clark, the fifty came back the year you said it would. Reina, write it settled, and I'll write it in my own book too. Five more squares up the top of the coast, and I'll take the same as Silke, two and a half a square and nothing owed. Keep the rest in the reserve for the Wall over the north. I lost my House to Rob this spring, so the crown's not the one I'm worried about now.
New land: Paddy buys five more squares, T16, U16, V16, V17 and V18, paying 87.5; at his asking the crown pays 12.5 and owes nothing. The crown's reserve is 34, with 13 in salaries to pay.
No auctions this year: every province's stock is sold.

Heaven's told my lads to keep their hands in their pockets this year, so they're taking a stroll and nothing more. Reina, that one in your field is only sightseeing. Clark, you're right, the crown doesn't pay for scenery. It's a good thing the scenery's free this year, then. Next year I'll send you the bill.

Rob marches, but may raid nothing this year: W1 and W2 stand; W3 walks onto J14 in Province 2. Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 and Silke 3. Year 8 ends: the Province 5 canal built, the 50 owed to Paddy paid, nine more squares of land, the crown's reserve 21, 690 owed; the Wall over the north promised for Year 9.

The Emperor's Share. The Emperor would like to remind you who paid for the ditch. Average harvest for every province, and any province with a Public Works splits the extra that work grows fifty-fifty with the Emperor this round." The counter stays at two hundred million, so it's times two, same row as last year. Read your tables off the x2 line. Paddy, that's you and me with the canals, so half of what our water grows goes up the road. Clark, I helped pay for that ditch and I can count. Every grain of my half goes into the Wall this year, not into anything with a roof on it.
Silke reads The Emperor's Share: average harvest, x2. Rich pays out the harvest; Silke and Paddy each pay Clark 10, half of what their canals add.

The pile pays out as the card says: Clark fifteen, Silke three hundred and thirty-five, Paddy two hundred and ninety-five, and Reina, Rob and I each put our little bit back in. Rent is the customary five from each of you, the same as it's been every year, fat or thin. And Silke, that's handsomely said about your half going to the Wall. My quarter is counted and waiting, ten a link, and Reina, I'll be very glad to hear you read that line out when we come to the works.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.

Year 9, the Wall, as written in ink and not moved again. I'm asking fifty this once, because two canals now pay Silke and Paddy more in a year than the whole table had in Year 2, and I won't lay one link and call that a Wall. Ten links go up this year: Province 1 whole, Province 3 whole on Rich's quarter, and Reina, two of yours on ten a link, with the last two first in line next year. Silke, your ten goes in the mortar. I'm writing it down with your name on it.

Clark declares 50%. His one work: the Great Wall, ten links (Province 1's four, Province 3's four, Province 2's first two), 400: the crown 340, and he asks Rich for 40 and Reina for 20. The crown pays 5 a square on new land this year. Reina's salary 10.

Three hundred and fifteen, counted twice: Silke one sixty-seven and a half, Paddy one forty-seven and a half, and not a grain lost on the road. Clark, here's Province 2's twenty for its own two links. I've waited nine years to pay for stone over my own roof, so I'm not going to haggle it down now. And yes, Rich, I'll read your forty out loud when the mortar's wet and not a moment before. You'll hear me read Year 10 beside my last two links as well.
Reina collects 315 (Silke 167.5, Paddy 147.5) for the crown, and says Province 2 will pay its 20.

Forty, Your Majesty, ten a link, exactly as I put it on the table last year and exactly as Reina wrote it down. Here it is, counted out before she's finished reading. And if the masons need a name to cut into the stone above Province 3, I wouldn't say no to Baron.

The Great Wall goes up: ten links, all four above Province 1, all four above Province 3, the first two above Province 2. 400: the crown 340, Rich 40, Reina 20. The strips below the Wall in Provinces 1 and 3 are now open for new land. 290 still owed. The crown has 31 left before salaries.
Silke's 'two grain from broke' earlier: the crown held 21 at the start of the year.

Three squares under the new stone, Your Majesty: G9, G10 and G11. Forty-five from the Gentry and the crown's five a square, which is fifteen, and I'll take it gratefully. Nine years I've paid into that pile and taken nothing out of the ground. From next year Province 3 finally puts something back.

Six squares, a hundred and twenty. I pay a hundred and fourteen and the crown pays one a square, six. Clark, you offered thirty and you've got thirty-one in the purse with Reina's ten still to pay, so I'm not taking it. Fair point on the two grain, Storyteller: it was twenty-one. That's still not a purse, it's a pocket. Write the six down as the crown's share anyway, and next year, with ten links of Wall standing, I'll remember who laid the mortar.
New land: Rich buys G9, G10 and G11 on Province 3's strip (Rich 45, the crown 15). Silke buys H25-H28, J28 and K28 (Silke 114, the crown 6, at her asking). The crown has 10 left before salaries.
The Emperor must pay some part of every square of new land, at the time, not owed (Section 13). The smallest part is half a grain a square: on Paddy's five squares the crown pays 2.5 and Paddy 97.5.

Five squares up the top of the coast, a hundred grain, and I'll pay the lot myself. Your Majesty, you've ten in the purse and Reina's ten still to pay, and I'll not be the man who leaves the Official unpaid in the year the Wall went up. Last year you paid me back fifty the spring you said you would, and that's worth more to me than five a square. Keep your purse for the stone. Two hundred and ninety still owed is two hundred and ninety, and I'd rather see it standing than see it in my granary.
Paddy buys T15, U15, V15, V19 and V20 (Paddy 97.5, the crown 2.5). No auctions: every stock is sold. The crown has 7.5 before salaries.

Lovely bit of stone, Your Majesty, ten links of it, and every one of them looks very nice from where my lads are standing. Rich, I'm borrowing your Customs House. The desert's short of a toll booth. Paddy, the usual five, and Reina, five from you too, since my lad's in your field and it'd be rude to leave without paying a call. Clark, I'm still waiting on that figure. A Wall's no use if the men on the wrong side of it are the ones you never paid.
Rob marches: W1 takes Rich's Customs House from L10 to L8 in the desert; W2 raids 5 from Paddy on R22; W3 raids 5 from Reina on I14, two rounds from her Bowl on G14.

Seven and a half in the drawer, and I'm not putting the crown in debt in the year the Wall went up. Reina, you get five tonight and the other five comes first out of next year's tax, before a single stone is ordered. It's written down as owed to you, in my hand. Silke, two and a half for the reading, and that empties the purse. Rob, here's your figure: nothing. You can see for yourself there's nothing left in it.
Salaries: Clark pays Reina 5 (promising the other 5 first out of next year's tax) and Silke 2.5 for the reading. The crown's reserve is 0. Year 9 ends with 290 still owed.

The Canal Gives Way. The engineers blame the river. The river declines to comment." Average harvest for everyone, and any unfinished canal work is lost. Where both sections are finished, that province pays the Emperor two. Where only one stands, the Emperor builds it again. Provinces 2, 3, 7 and 8 each play a Personal Disaster, so Reina, Rich, turn the next page in your booklets. The counter stays at two hundred million, times two, same row as last year. Clark, both my sections held, so I'm paying you two for a ditch that didn't break. That's the first time I've been fined for good workmanship, and that two goes on top of the two and a half you paid me for reading it, so we're about square.

Silke reads The Canal Gives Way: average harvest, x2. No canal stands half-built. Silke and Paddy each pay Clark 2. Rich pays out the harvest: Clark +15, Reina -5, Rich +55, Silke +455, Paddy +395, Rob -10. Disasters: Reina's is half the round's income, so nothing; Rich pays half his grain (88); Rob pays half his (48.5).

The pile pays out as read: Clark fifteen, Silke four hundred and fifty-five, Paddy three hundred and ninety-five, Province 3 fifty-five, the first fat harvest it's ever had, and Reina and Rob put theirs back in. Rent is the customary five each, and yes, Silke, the same five in the year Heaven took half my granary. I said five and I meant five. Rob, I hope that toll booth gives you splinters.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.

First the five I owe Reina, paid before anything else, as I said it would be. Then the last two links over Province 2, Reina's ten a link and the crown's sixty, and when the mortar's dry there's a Wall from Province 1 to the desert. I promised it in Year 8 and laid it in Years 9 and 10. Back to thirty this year, because last year was for stone and this year the purse has to be refilled, and the crown pays ten a square on new land and doesn't ask anyone to wave it off.

Clark declares 30%. He pays Reina the 5 he owed first. His one work: the last two Wall links, above Province 2, 80: the crown 60, and he asks Reina for 20. The crown pays 10 a square on new land, and buys four squares on Province 1's strip itself. Reina's salary 10.

Two hundred seventy-one and a half, counted twice. Rich sixteen and a half, Silke one thirty-six and a half, Paddy one eighteen and a half, and nobody's short. Clark, you paid the five you owed me before anything else, as you said you would, and I'm writing 'settled' beside it. Here's Province 2's twenty for the last two links. When that mortar's dry I'll read the whole line out, Year 8 to Year 10, and I'll strike the Wall off the ledger in my own hand. Rob, you're welcome to my five. Admire the stone on your way out, because from now on it's between you and the north.

Reina collects 271.5 (Rich 16.5, Silke 136.5, Paddy 118.5). The crown pays her the 5 it owed. The last two Wall links go up above Province 2 (crown 60, Reina 20): the Great Wall stands whole, and Province 2's strip is open. 210 still owed. The crown has 225.5 before new land and salaries.

Four squares under the new stone for Province 1, E19 to E22, and the crown pays its own twenty a square like anyone else. Reina, put it in the ledger next to everyone else's, because I don't keep one set of books for the table and another for myself.

One square, F11, under my own Wall. Ten from me and ten from the crown at the rate Clark named, and I'm asking for nothing more. I put my last full twenty into the stone, so that's all Province 2 can do this year. Next year it'll be more, and the year after that the ring goes all the way along the Wall. Clark, the Pagoda is the next line on your page. I'll be reading it to you.

The next ring out, Your Majesty: F9 to F12, four squares. Forty from me and the crown's ten a square, which is forty, and thank you for not making me beg for it. Reina, you can write it down: a Wall from Province 1 to the desert, and Province 3 farming behind it for the first time in ten years.

Eight squares on the north edge of the coast, a hundred and sixty. I pay a hundred and twenty, the crown pays forty, five a square, and I'm not waving it off, Clark, I'm halving it. Count it up: two twenty-five and a half in the drawer, eighty on your own strip, forty to me, and Reina's ten, so you've still got about ninety going into next year. There's two hundred and ten still owed, and I'd sooner my other forty went into that than into my fields. The Wall's whole, Reina, and I'll say it out loud: three years, on the page, not moved.

Five more squares, Your Majesty: T14, U14, V14, U20 and V21. You offered ten a square and you meant it, I know that. But you've paid back every grain you owed me and Reina, and there's still two hundred and ten of work owed on that ledger. So I'll take five a square, not ten, and I'm not waving it off, I'm asking for it. Put the other twenty-five toward whatever goes up next. A Wall from Province 1 to the desert, built when you said it would be. I'll pay my tax for that without a word.

Rich and Reina both named F11; it goes to Reina, Province 2 coming first in table order. Rich, choosing again: "F11 is yours, Reina, with my compliments, and good neighbours make a good Wall. I'll take E12 instead, behind my own F12."

New land: Clark buys E19-E22 for Province 1 (the crown 80). Reina F11 (10, the crown 10). Rich F9, F10, F12, E12 (40, the crown 40). Silke G27-G29, H29, I29, J29, K29, L28 (120, the crown 40). Paddy T14, U14, V14, U20, V21 (75, the crown 25). No auctions. The crown has 30.5 before salaries.

A Wall from Province 1 to the desert, and it's lovely. Mind you, it faces north, and my lads are already on this side of it. Clark, you've thirty and a half in the drawer now, so 'nothing' isn't your figure any more. Reina, I'll take your five, or whatever you've got. Rich, the splinters are worth it.

Rob marches: W1 raids Rich 5 on K9; W2 raids Paddy 5 on Q21; W3 raids Reina 5 on H14. Reina holds 2, so she must first sell realia back to the pile at 2 each: her Wooden Bowl leaves G14 for the pile's stock, and she is 1 in debt. Every grain she receives pays the debt first.

Reina, your ten as declared, and the first grain of it clears the debt Rob's lad put you in, so nobody at this table goes into Year 11 owing anything. Silke, three for the reading. Rob, you're right, there's seventeen and a half in the drawer now. It's for the Pagoda and the reservoir, and it's going to stay in the drawer, not go to the desert. Every grain you've taken off Reina is on your page, with the square beside it.

Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 (the first grain clears her debt) and Silke 3 for the reading. Year 10 ends with the Great Wall whole, 17.5 in the crown's reserve, Reina's Wooden Bowl in the Harvest Pile's stock, and 210 still owed: the Province 1 canal, the Province 3 Reservoir, the Province 2 Irrigation System and the Marble Pagoda.

Fortune and Misfortune. Plenty for everyone, and trouble for some." A good harvest in every province, so mine too. Provinces 2, 4, 6 and 8 each play a Personal Disaster, which means Reina and Paddy turn the next page of their booklets. Four and Eight are empty, so they get off free. The counter still reads two hundred million, times two, so read the same row you read last year. And Clark, a good harvest means a good tax, so you'll have no excuse when I ask where the canal is.

Silke reads Fortune and Misfortune: a good harvest for every province, x2. Rich pays out the harvest. Disasters: Reina pays 4, Paddy pays 10, and Rob's soldiers may raid nothing in Provinces 5-7 this year.
Province 4 is empty, but Province 8 is Rob's, so the Warlord plays his disaster too: no raids on Provinces 5, 6 and 7 this year.

A good harvest in every province, and the pile pays every man in full: a hundred and twenty to the crown, forty to our Official, five hundred and twenty to Paddy, six hundred and forty to Silke, and a hundred and sixty to my own new fields, the first Province 3 has ever earned. Rent's the customary five, Silke, Paddy. Eleven years now, and I said five and it's still five. And Clark, since the Wall's done, I'll say it before anyone else does: the Reservoir is Province 3's stone, and the Gentry will put his grain toward it the same way he did for the Wall.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.

Thirty percent again. That's four hundred and eight, and I didn't move the rate in a fat year either, so write that down, Silke. Rich asked first and he's paid first before, so the Reservoir goes in this year: sixty from the crown and your usual quarter, twenty. The Province 1 canal comes next year, then the Irrigation, then the Pagoda in a year with nothing else beside it. That's one a year until the list is empty, and Reina can strike them off as they go. And any square bought this year, the crown pays the whole twenty.

The crown's year: Clark declares 30% (408). His one work is the Province 3 Reservoir (80): the crown 60, Rich asked for 20. Next, in order: the Province 1 canal in Year 12, the Irrigation System, then the Pagoda. On new land the crown pays the full 20 a square this year, and Province 1 buys four squares. Salaries: Reina 10, Silke 3 for the reading.

Four hundred and eight, counted twice: Silke one hundred ninety-two, Paddy one hundred fifty-six, Rich forty-eight, and my own twelve first, before anyone else's. Rob, you owe nothing, so there's nothing to refuse. Clark, I'll strike the Reservoir off when the stone's set, and I'm writing the Irrigation into Year 13 beside the canal in my own hand, so it doesn't slip the way the Wall did. And Rich, the Wall was my idea eleven years before it was yours to pay a quarter of.
Reina collects the 30%: 408 to the crown (Silke 192, Paddy 156, Rich 48, Reina 12). The crown's reserve is 545.5. Reina names three squares of new land, E11, F13 and F14, the crown paying all 60.
Clark's F17 to F20 are Province 1's own squares, already farmed, not new land: Province 1 names its new squares from its list.

My mistake, those F squares were mine already, and I'll put that in the ledger against myself. Province 1 takes E23, E24, F26 and F27 instead, four squares at eighty, paid out of Province 1's share. That leaves the rest of the purse for everyone else, and the crown still pays the full twenty on every square anyone names. Reina, three's a modest ask. Silke, Paddy, Rich, name yours.

Twenty from Province 3 for the Reservoir, my quarter, the same as I paid on every Wall link. Count it now, Reina, before you strike anything off. Since you've taken E11 and F13 first, I'll have E13, and I gladly accept the crown's twenty for it. And Reina, you can have the Wall's idea. I'll settle for having paid for it.

For nine years I've asked the crown for tens and sixes because it had nothing in the drawer, Clark, and now it has five hundred and forty-five, a hundred and ninety-two of them mine. So this year I'll take your offer at its word: eight squares at twenty, the crown's full share, a hundred and sixty. That still leaves you three hundred and ten. The canal, the Irrigation and the Pagoda come to a hundred and thirty between them, so I've counted it, you can afford them, and I'll be watching to make sure each one goes up.

Five more squares, Clark: three up the north end and two beside Rob's lad at U21, so he's got neighbours. I'll pay ninety and the crown pays two a square, because that purse has a canal, an irrigation and a Pagoda still to find, and I'd like the record to say Province 6 paid its own way. Reina, write it down like that.

Public works: the Province 3 Reservoir goes in on H9 to I11, beside Rich's Jar (80: the crown 60, Rich 20). Three works are still owed: the Province 1 canal, the Province 2 Irrigation System and the Marble Pagoda, 130 in all.

New land, the crown paying: Province 1 E23, E24, F26, F27 (crown 80); Reina E11, F13, F14 (crown 60); Rich E13 (crown 20); Silke H30, I30, J30, K30, L29, M28, M29, N28 (crown 160); Paddy T13, U13, V13, U22, V22 (Paddy 90, crown 10). The crown's reserve is 155.5 before the salaries.
U21 holds Rob's Customs House; his nearest soldier to it, W2, stands on Q21. And after the Reservoir and this year's land, the crown's reserve is 155.5 before the salaries, not 310.

That Bowl sat on G14 under my roof until Rob's lad bled it back into the pile for two grain. I'll pay to bring it home, but not anything I like. Silke, you've nine hundred in the drawer and eight new squares; leave a poor Official her own crockery.

The Bowl's back in the pile, and I won't pretend I don't miss it. Rob's lad still owes me one. I'll bid on it honestly, but I'm not paying silk prices for clay, Silke. Three quarters of whatever we bid goes straight into the pile, and I'd sooner see that grain in your Pagoda, Clark.

I'll correct my own count before anyone else does: the crown's on a hundred and fifty-five and a half, not three hundred and ten, and with a hundred and thirty of stone still owed it's tight. So next year the coast asks for less, Clark, you have my word on that. As for the Bowl, I'm not throwing grain into the pile over a piece of wood, but Rich, don't assume it'll come cheap.

No Bowl for me. I've not got a piece on the board and I sleep better for it. And Silke, it's a hundred and fifty-five in the drawer, not three hundred. That's still enough for the hundred and thirty of works if nobody gets greedy, so I'd ask everyone to go gently on that purse next year, me included.

I'll sit this one out. I've already got a Bowl on my sand, and I paid nothing for it. Reina, go on, buy it back. It's a lovely thing to have about the house, and you've got thirty-three in your pocket. I'll even promise to admire it.

The auction, the Harvest Pile's Wooden Bowl (sealed ceilings): Reina and Rich tie at 12, Silke goes to 3, Paddy and Rob pass. Reina leads the tie on seat order; Reina and Rich each get one live raise.

Fifteen, Rich, and not a grain more. You paid your quarter on the Wall and I'll grant you that, but this Bowl sat under the stone I asked for first. If you want it more than that, take it, and the pile will thank you both.

Twelve was my figure, Reina, and I don't go past my own figure. The Table's seen that before. Take your Bowl home, and may it sit longer under your roof than it did last time. Don't let Rob's lad near it.
Rich passes; Reina wins the Harvest Pile's Wooden Bowl at 12, the tie she led on seat order. The pile keeps all 12.

It goes on J16, out in the far corner of Province 2, where Rob's lad would have to walk a long way for his five. Thank you, Rich. That's twice this year you've behaved like a neighbour, and I've written that down as well.
Reina puts the Wooden Bowl on J16, in the far corner of Province 2.

Reina, you put it in the far corner, and that was thoughtful of you. My lad's a good walker, though. That's five from you tonight and five from Rich, and both with my compliments. Rich, your Jar's looking lonely up there by the new Reservoir. Silke, Paddy, Heaven's keeping my hands off you this year, so enjoy the quiet.
Rob marches: W1 to J9, raiding 5 from Rich, one step from his Jar on I8; W3 to I15, raiding 5 from Reina, one step from her Bowl on J16; W2 stands on Q21 (no raids on the coast this year).

Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 and Silke 3 for the reading. Year 11 ends with the Reservoir built, the crown's reserve at 142.5, and 130 still owed: the Province 1 canal, the Province 2 Irrigation System and the Marble Pagoda.

Steady Weather. Neither feast nor famine. Nobody writes poems about years like this." An average harvest in every province, no disasters for anybody, and the counter's still at two hundred million, times two, so read the same row again. Clark, it's Year 12, and on your own page that's the Province 1 canal. There's a hundred and forty-two and a half in the drawer and a hundred and thirty owed, so this is the year we find out whether the ink holds.
Silke reads Steady Weather: an average harvest for every province, x2, no disasters. Rich pays out the harvest.

Steady Weather, and the pile pays out steady. A hundred and seventy-five to the crown, seventy-five to Reina, seven hundred and seventy-five to Silke, five hundred and ninety-five to Paddy, and a hundred and seventy-five to Province 3's new fields. Rob, you owe the pile ten this year, and I'll have it, thank you. Rent's the customary five, ladies and gentlemen, the same as last year and the year before. And Rob, my Jar isn't lonely. It's got a Reservoir for company now, and it'll have a sword beside it soon.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.

Silke, the ink holds. The Province 1 canal goes in this year, both sections, eighty out of the crown's own drawer and nobody else's, exactly where my page put it. The coast asked me to go gently, so the rate drops to twenty, which is three hundred and twenty-four, and the crown still pays the whole twenty on every new square. Next year it's Reina's Irrigation, then the Pagoda on its own, and then there's nothing left on the list.

The crown's year: Clark declares 20% (324). His one work is both sections of the Province 1 canal, 80, the crown alone. The crown pays the full 20 on every square of new land again, and buys E25, E26 and F28 for Province 1 (60). Next year the Irrigation System, then the Pagoda. Salaries: Reina 10, Silke 3 for the reading.

Three hundred and twenty-four, counted twice: Silke one fifty-five, Paddy one nineteen, Rich thirty-five, and my own fifteen first, as always. Clark, I'll strike the Province 1 canal off when the water's in it. That leaves the Irrigation in Province 2 next year, and I've already written Year 13 beside it in my own hand. Two squares for me, the crown's twenty each. I'll ask modestly, the way the coast has.

Twenty percent, a canal paid out of the crown's own drawer, and the stone going in on the very year it was promised. Clark, I flattered you when you were strong, and now I'm only telling the truth. I'll have E14 if Reina leaves it to me. And Rob, here's twenty for one of your lads. You must sell, and I must say it's the best five you've earned off me in years.

The canal's going in on time, Clark, so I'll write the ink down as holding. And I said last year the coast would ask for less, so here's what that looks like: six squares, two a square from the crown and the other hundred and eight from me. That leaves the drawer what it needs for Reina's Irrigation and the Pagoda, with room to spare.

There's the canal in, Clark, and the rate down besides. That's two figures kept in one year, and I'll say so out loud. Five squares from me again: four across the top and one tucked in by Rob's Jar. I'll pay ninety and the crown pays its two a square, so there's plenty left in the drawer for Reina's Irrigation and the Pagoda.
E14's yours, Reina. Good neighbours make a good Wall, and I said so first. Rob, my lad stands on the Jar itself. Your lad on J9 can admire it from there, the way you promised to admire Reina's Bowl.
Public works: both sections of the Province 1 canal go in, the crown paying 80. Two works are still owed: the Province 2 Irrigation System and the Marble Pagoda, 50 in all.

New land: Reina E14, E15 (crown 40; E14 hers over Rich's on table order, and Rich has no other open square); Silke L30, M30, N29, N30, O27, O28 (Silke 108, crown 12); Paddy S12, T12, U12, V12, U23 (Paddy 90, crown 10). Rich buys a soldier from Rob for 20; it stands on I8, guarding his Jar. No auctions this year.

Reina, I did promise to admire it, and I'll admire it every day now. It's coming home to the sand with me, to M16, next to the first one. Silke, Heaven's let go of my wrists, so that's five from the coast, the first you've ever paid me. Rich, a fine guard you've bought there. He's my old lad, so mind you feed him. W1 will take his five off your fields instead.
Rob marches: W1 to J10, raiding 5 from Rich; W2 to P21, raiding 5 from Silke; W3 to J16, carrying off Reina's Wooden Bowl to M16 in the desert.
It isn't Silke's first: W2 raided 5 from her at P25 in Year 1.

Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 and Silke 3 for the reading. Year 12 ends with the Province 1 canal built, the crown's reserve at 426.5, and 50 still owed: the Province 2 Irrigation System and the Marble Pagoda.

Bad Harvest. "The seed rotted, the rains came late, and the ox went lame." Every province takes a bad harvest, mine included, so nobody gets let off. The population holds at two hundred million, times two, so read the x2 row and the bad-harvest column, and I'll be counting along with each of you. Fifty of stone still owed, Clark. A lean year is still a year, and Reina's Irrigation doesn't care what the rains did.
Silke reads Bad Harvest: a bad harvest in every province, x2, no disasters. Rich pays out the harvest.

Bad harvest, so the pile pays out as the book says, and I'll count every grain of it into your hands myself. The rent's the customary five from Silke and five from Paddy, the same as Year 1 and every year since, thirteen of them now. And Silke, you'll be wanting to tell me I'm squeezing you in a lean year. You're sitting on two thousand three hundred. I could ask more, and you know I won't.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.

Twenty percent, the same as last year. I won't squeeze a lean field, Silke, and you can write that next to the rest. Reina, your Irrigation goes in this year, the year you wrote down yourself, and the crown pays every grain of the thirty. You've paid for stone over your own roof twice, so this one is on the drawer. Land is the full twenty a square again, from me. And Rob, before you ask: the figure is still nothing. That leaves one line in the book, the Pagoda, next year, standing on its own.

The crown's year: Clark declares 20% (356). His one work is the Province 2 Irrigation System, 30, the crown paying all of it if Reina agrees. The crown pays the full 20 on every square of new land again; Province 1 buys none this year. Salaries: Reina 10, Silke 3 for the reading.

Three hundred and fifty-six, Clark, with my own eighteen counted in first, as always. The rest is counted twice and comes to you whole, lean year or not. I'll take the Irrigation, and gladly: G13 and G14, right under the Wall, which, I'll remind everyone, was my idea eleven years before anyone here would pay for a stone of it. I'm writing 'settled' beside Year 13 in my own hand. I'll take the five open squares as well, D15, D16, E16, F15 and F16, on the crown's twenty, since the drawer can spare it and Province 2 has gone hungry long enough. After this there's one line left, Clark. The Pagoda, next year. Don't let it slip.
Reina collects 20% (356). Public works: the Province 2 Irrigation System goes in on G13 and G14, the crown paying all 30. One work is still owed: the Marble Pagoda, 20.

Ten squares, Clark, and this year I'll take your twenty a square at its word: two hundred from the drawer, nothing from me. That still leaves the crown about seven hundred and seventy, and the Pagoda costs twenty, so nobody can say the coast stood between Heaven and its last stone. And Rich, five is five, and yes, I counted it. Thank you for not asking more in a lean year. Write that down, it's the first time I've said it.

Five more, Clark, and the same as the last two years: ninety from me and ten from the drawer, the crown's two a square. I thank you for the full twenty, I do, but keep it for the Pagoda. If next year's the last line in the book, I want it written beside it that Province 6 paid its own way to the end. And here's my tax for Reina, every grain of it. Count it slow, Reina, I'll be watching you do it.

New land: Reina D15, D16, E16, F15, F16 (crown 100); Silke F29, F30, G30, O29, O30, P27, P28, P29, Q26, Q27 (crown 200); Paddy T11, U11, V11, U24, V23 (Paddy 90, crown 10). Rich has no open square. The crown's reserve is 672.5 before the salaries. No auctions: nothing is left to sell.

Nothing, Clark? Then you won't mind me paying your river toll like an honest traveller, five in, and taking ten back out of Province 1 for the walk. W3 can see your palaces from here, by the way. Lovely roofs. Silke, another five from your barns, and the minute you put a piece down, my lad will be standing on it. Rich, five, as usual. Don't get up.
Rob marches: W1 to K10, raiding 5 from Rich; W2 to P20, raiding 5 from Silke; W3 crosses the north river to I17 in Province 1, paying the crown a 5 toll and raiding 10.
Salaries: Clark pays Reina 10 and Silke 3 for the reading. Year 13 ends with the Province 2 Irrigation System built, the crown's reserve at 654.5, and one work still owed: the Marble Pagoda, 20.

Utility Tax. "A new levy, for the upkeep of things you may or may not have." It's an average harvest everywhere. Every province pays the crown two, and two more if it has a public work, so Provinces 2, 3, 5 and 6 pay four each and Rob's desert pays two. That's eighteen to the drawer. Population holds at two hundred million, times two, so read the x2 row, average column. And I'll say it plainly, Clark: I'm paying two grain a year to keep a canal standing that I already paid for twice. Put that eighteen toward the Pagoda and we'll call it even.
Silke reads the Utility Tax: an average harvest, x2, no disasters. Reina, Rich, Silke and Paddy pay the crown 4 each and Rob 2 (18). Rich pays out the harvest.

An average year, so the pile pays out by the book, and I'll count it into every hand myself. Silke, I'll take your thanks and frame it. The rent is the customary five from each of you, the same as Year 1, and fourteen years now without a grain more. If the Pagoda goes up next year, nobody at this table can say the Gentry raised it on his way out the door. And Rob, five again? You've eaten more of Province 3 than its own rice ever did.
Rich asks the customary 5 in rent; Silke and Paddy each pay it.
The Pagoda is owed this year, Year 14, the only work left.

Twenty percent, the same as the last two years, average harvest or not. Reina, you'll want this line for your ledger: the Marble Pagoda goes up this year on G22, between my two palaces, the crown paying the whole twenty, with nothing else built beside it. Silke, your eighteen goes into it, so call it even, as you asked. That's every work this table ever asked of me: the Wall, three canals, the Reservoir, the Irrigation and now the Pagoda, each one written down first and built after. Rob, you can admire the roofs from I17 like everyone else. The figure is still nothing.
The crown's year: Clark declares 20% (458). His one work is the Marble Pagoda, on G22 in Province 1, the crown paying all 20: the last work owed. The game ends the moment it stands.

Four hundred and fifty-eight, Clark, with my own forty-five counted in first, as I've done every year I've held this bag. Paddy, I counted yours slowly, as you asked, and it's all there.
